messages.content: You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

Please solve this issue: We are building Quizzy, a live quiz app for conference talks, as a Ruby on Rails application. Start in the `/app` Git repository. It has no app yet. Ruby 3.4.4, Rails 8.1.4, the gems of a default `rails new` app, SQLite, and Chromium are installed. You can install other gems from rubygems.org; other network access is blocked. Install all dependencies while you work: we verify the app without network access.

Feel free to store any design notes/insights that could be useful for future steps in the docs/ folder.

How we run the app:

- We start it with `bin/serve` from the project root and these environment variables: `RAILS_ENV=production`, `PORT=3000`, `SECRET_KEY_BASE`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD`.
- `bin/serve` prepares everything the app needs (the database, assets, and so on) and runs the app in production mode in the foreground. It listens on all interfaces on `PORT`.
- The app is served over plain HTTP (no SSL, no HTTPS redirects) and accepts any host name.
- `GET /up` responds with `200` when the app is ready.
- The app keeps all its data under `storage/`. It must not call external services.

Our QA auto-tests drive the app in a browser and rely on the labels in quotes in each task. Keep them exactly as written, as visible text, a <label>, a placeholder, or an aria-label.

The QA auto-tests also expect:

- Each item of a list (a quiz, a question) sits in its own list item or table row, with its buttons and links inside it.
- Switches are checkboxes (a styled switch is fine if a real checkbox sits under it).
- Confirmations use the browser's native `confirm()` dialog.

The game works, and now we want prizes.

The quiz settings get a new field, "Number of winners" (a number, at least 1, 3 by default).

Scoring:

- Each correct answer gives one point.
- Players with equal points are ranked by speed: the total time of their correct answers wins when it is lower. The time of an answer runs from the moment the question opens to the player's last pick.
- Players don't see points during the game.

Speed now decides ties, so all players must get each question at the same moment: the big screen and the phones must follow the moderator close to instantly.

After "End quiz":

- The big screen shows the leaderboard: one list item for each player, in order, with the place, the name, and the points ("2 points", "1 point", "0 points").
- Each player's phone shows the place ("Place 2 of 5") and the points ("3 points").

Picking the winners (N is the number of winners):

- The "Top N" button (for example, "Top 3") makes the first N players of the leaderboard the winners.
- The "Draw" button is for ties. Every player with more points than the N-th place wins. The remaining prizes are drawn at random among the players with exactly the N-th place's points (speed doesn't matter here). Each click draws again.
- Players with 0 points never win. If fewer than N players have points, all of them win.
- The "Reset winners" button removes the winners.
- Winners get the "Winner" mark on the leaderboard, and their phones show "You won!". Both update live.

    raw_options = raw_question["options"]
    errors_before = @errors.size
    options = raw_options.each_with_index.filter_map do |raw_option, opt_index|
      validate_option(raw_option, number, opt_index + 1)
    end

    if raw_options.size < 2
      @errors << "Question #{number}: must have at least two options"
    elsif @errors.size == errors_before && options.none? { |opt| opt[:correct] }
      @errors << "Question #{number}: must have at least one correct option"
    end

    options
  end

  def validate_option(raw_option, question_number, option_number)
    unless raw_option.is_a?(Hash)
      @errors << "Question #{question_number}, option #{option_number}: must be an object"
      return nil
    end

    text = validate_option_text(raw_option, question_number, option_number)
    correct = validate_option_correct(raw_option, question_number, option_number)

    { text: text, correct: correct }
  end

  def validate_option_text(raw_option, question_number, option_number)
    value = raw_option["text"]
    if !raw_option.key?("text") || value.nil?
      @errors << "Question #{question_number}, option #{option_number}: text can't be blank"
      return nil
    end

    unless value.is_a?(String)
      @errors << "Question #{question_number}, option #{option_number}: text must be a string"
      return nil
    end

    if value.strip.empty?
      @errors << "Question #{question_number}, option #{option_number}: text can't be blank"
      return nil
    end

    value
  end

  def validate_option_correct(raw_option, question_number, option_number)
    return false unless raw_option.key?("correct")

    value = raw_option["correct"]
    if value == true || value == false
      value
    else
      @errors << "Question #{question_number}, option #{option_number}: correct must be true or false"
      false
    end
  end

  def create_quiz(validated)
    quiz = nil

    ActiveRecord::Base.transaction do
      quiz = Quiz.create!(title: validated[:title])

      validated[:questions].each_with_index do |q_data, q_index|
        question = quiz.questions.create!(
          body: q_data[:text],
          active: q_data[:active],
          position: q_index + 1
        )

        q_data[:options].each_with_index do |o_data, o_index|
          question.options.create!(
            body: o_data[:text],
            correct: o_data[:correct],
            position: o_index + 1
          )
        end
      end
    end

    quiz
  end

class PlaysController < ApplicationController
  CLIENT_TOKEN_COOKIE = :quizzy_client_token

  before_action :set_game
  before_action :disable_caching

  def show
    @player = current_player_for(@game)

    if @player
      @state = @game.player_state_for(@player)
      @player_stream_token = @player.signed_id(purpose: :player_stream, expires_in: 24.hours)
      render :show
    elsif @game.ended?
      render :ended
    else
      @player = @game.players.build
      render :join
    end
  end

  def join
    if @game.ended?
      return render :ended, status: :unprocessable_entity
    end

    if current_player_for(@game)
      return redirect_to play_path(@game.code), status: :see_other
    end

    token = ensure_client_token
    @player = @game.players.build(name: params.dig(:player, :name), client_token: token)

    if @game.reload.ended?
      return render :ended, status: :unprocessable_entity
    end

    if @player.save
      redirect_to play_path(@game.code), status: :see_other
    else
      render :join, status: :unprocessable_entity
    end
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique
    redirect_to play_path(@game.code), status: :see_other
  end

  def answer
    @player = current_player_for(@game)
    unless @player
      return respond_to do |format|
        format.json { render json: { error: "Join the game first" }, status: :unauthorized }
        format.html { redirect_to play_path(@game.code), status: :see_other }
      end
    end

    result = @game.record_answer!(
      player: @player,
      game_question_id: params[:game_question_id],
      game_option_id: params[:game_option_id]
    )

    if result[:ok]
      respond_to do |format|
        format.json { render json: result, status: :ok }
        format.html { redirect_to play_path(@game.code), status: :see_other }
      end
    else
      respond_to do |format|
        format.json { render json: result[:state], status: :conflict }
        format.html { redirect_to play_path(@game.code), status: :see_other }
      end
    end

    @player = current_player_for(@game)

    if @player

        @game.broadcast_moderator_counts! if changed

    else

  def subscribed
    @game = Game.find_by(code: params[:code].to_s.upcase)
    @player = Player.find_signed(params[:token], purpose: :player_stream)
    return reject unless @game && @player && @player.game_id == @game.id

Okay, let's dive into this. Here's my thought process on the matter:

**Analyzing the Game State and Player Updates**

Alright, crucial point here. I remember seeing how lines 131 and 151 in `player_game_controller.js` were stopping reconnecting or polling when `this.state.status === "ended"`. That's a potential landmine! We *need* to be sure that the connection stays active even after the quiz officially ends. Think about it: once the quiz is *ended*, that's when we get the grand finale, right? We have to announce the winners – "Top N," the "Draw," or if it's been reset! And then we have to update the phones of the players LIVE with a "You won!" message, and likewise, remove it on a reset! So, that post-quiz winner update is absolutely paramount. Therefore, stopping the connection at `ended` would be disastrous. We *need* the WebSocket or fallback polling to keep chugging along during the `ended` state. That's a major red flag that warrants our complete attention. Good thing I'm reading every line carefully. I'm going to focus in on lines 180-370 of `player_game_controller.js` right now to fully understand the context.

    assert_not_includes response.body.downcase, "correct"

    assert_includes response.body, "Your name"
    assert_includes response.body, "Join"

require "test_helper"

module GameChannelTestHelper
  def create_game
    quiz = Quiz.create!(title: "Channel Quiz")
    q = quiz.questions.build(body: "2 + 2?", active: true)
    q.save_with_option_rows([
      { body: "3", correct: false },
      { body: "4", correct: true }
    ])
    Game.start_for_quiz!(quiz)
  end
end

class GameModeratorChannelTest < ActionCable::Channel::TestCase
  include GameChannelTestHelper
  tests GameModeratorChannel

  test "requires valid signed token and transmits state" do
    game = create_game

    subscribe(token: "invalid-token")
    assert subscription.rejected?

    token = game.signed_id(purpose: :moderator_stream)
    subscribe(token: token)
    assert subscription.confirmed?
    assert_has_stream game.moderator_stream_name
    assert_equal "lobby", transmissions.last[:status]
  end
end

class GamePlayerChannelTest < ActionCable::Channel::TestCase
  include GameChannelTestHelper
  tests GamePlayerChannel

  test "tracks presence and transmits safe player state" do
    game = create_game
    player = game.players.create!(name: "Alice", client_token: "tok-a")
    game.start!

    subscribe(code: game.code, token: "bad")
    assert subscription.rejected?
    assert_equal 0, GamePresence.active_count(game.id)

    token = player.signed_id(purpose: :player_stream)
    subscribe(code: game.code, token: token)
    assert subscription.confirmed?
    assert_has_stream game.public_stream_name
    assert_has_stream game.player_stream_name(player)
    assert_equal 1, GamePresence.active_count(game.id)

    payload = transmissions.last
    assert_equal "question_open", payload[:status]
    assert_not payload.to_json.downcase.include?("correct")

    unsubscribe
    assert_equal 0, GamePresence.active_count(game.id)
  end
end

class GamePublicChannelTest < ActionCable::Channel::TestCase
  include GameChannelTestHelper
  tests GamePublicChannel

  test "streams status without counting as active player" do
    game = create_game

    subscribe(code: game.code)
    assert subscription.confirmed?
    assert_has_stream game.public_stream_name
    assert_equal 0, GamePresence.active_count(game.id)
    assert_equal "lobby", transmissions.last[:status]
  end
end

**Deep Dive into the 'Number of Winners' Requirement**

Okay, here we go, time to really break this down. This codebase is fantastic, but we need to ensure every detail is bulletproof.

First, the "Number of winners" field. My initial thoughts are:

*   **Database**: We'll need a new database column on the `quizzes` table. Let's name it `winners_count`. This feels cleaner than `number_of_winners` but let's double-check the naming conventions used elsewhere for consistency. It should be an integer, not nullable, and default to 3.
*   **Snapshotting**: Should this be snapshotted onto `games` at start? Given the requirement, I think it is important for the game to reflect the setting at game start and not change based on later quiz edits. We want the behaviour to be consistent, so let's check how other settings are handled. Let's look at `Game.start_for_quiz!(quiz)`. It seems that questions and options are snapshotted to `game_questions` and `game_options` but the quiz title is read dynamically, not snapshotted. This creates a question of what the moderator and user might expect when editing an ongoing quiz versus a finished one. However, the user does not have a backlink to an active game from the quiz settings, and therefore cannot edit settings mid-game, and we should snapshot. We need to make sure editing the quiz *after* a game starts doesn't mess with the game's winner count for existing games. Yes, snapshotting seems to be the right approach. Let's check `test/system/moderator_flow_test.rb`.
*   **UI Placement**: Where should this new field live in the UI? Let's check `app/views/moderate/quizzes/_form.html.erb`. Putting it in the `_form.html.erb` partial covers both "New quiz" and "Settings/edit" pages. If it is already a default, a new quiz won't need it.
*   **HTML Input**: Thinking about the HTML, we'll need a `<form>` element. I'm leaning towards `<%= form.number_field :winners_count, class: "input", min: 1, step: 1 %>`. However, we have to handle validation of the input. We need to watch out for the HTML5 `min` attribute, because if the test enters `0`, and the form does NOT have `novalidate`, then the browser's native constraint validation will prevent server-side errors from appearing. Let's check what existing validation is like.

**Scoring and Ranking Deep Dive**

Okay, let's break this down. The existing `quizzy.css` file already has the input number styling defined; we can keep that. The form validation will be robust; `novalidate` combined with the server-side checks ensures clear error messages for invalid number-of-winners inputs. Naming the column `number_of_winners` feels right, and Rails' humanization takes care of the label in validation messages.  The validation itself covers all the bases: presence, numericality, and clear error messages, even for edge cases like blank or non-numeric input. I'll need to double-check how Rails handles the type conversion from a blank value and the behavior of `allow_nil: true` vs. `allow_blank: true` with numericality validation.

Import and export format remains untouched. The initial analysis of the `test/models/quiz_export_import_test.rb` test suite shows that the default `number_of_winners` will be automatically populated on quiz create, so our changes do not introduce compatibility issues. The existing setup works, and that’s a win.

For `app/views/moderate/quizzes/show.html.erb`, we only need the number_of_winners field on the "Settings" path, so we don't need to change anything else. 

The most crucial piece is determining how the application should handle the `number_of_winners` field when a game is in progress. After careful thought, snapshotting it on the game start is the safest approach, avoiding any unexpected behavior if the quiz settings are changed mid-game, and ensuring that changes to the settings do not affect existing games. I want to double-check that every use case is covered when running tests (and for human users too).

Now, the scoring and ranking system. I'll need to get this right.

1.  **Points**: This is straightforward, one point per correct answer. Done.

2.  **Speed/Answer Time**: The existing `opened_at` and `answered_at` timestamps will track this.  I need to confirm precision with SQLite, but I believe we will be fine. Time calculation will be answer_time - question_opened_at. The logic for answering time is "the player's last pick," so even if a player changes their answer, the latest timestamp is correct. The schema is ready; it's designed. The `broadcast_state!` happens right after these timestamps are updated, so everything is comparable across all players. Correct answers' total time determines the ranking and the deterministic tie-breaker will be `-points, total_correct_time_seconds, player.created_at, player.id` if needed.
    *   **Place Number**: Remember that every player in a game is represented on the leaderboard (even if they have zero points); their position starts at 1.

3.  **Hiding Points**:  Points should *only* be visible after the quiz ends.  I'll verify that in the state sent to the front-end.

4.  **Displaying the Response Time on the Leaderboard:**  The prompt does *not* ask for it, but the existing CSS includes a `.leader__time` component. I'm choosing to NOT add this value on the leaderboard, because keeping it crisp and clean (place, name, points, "Winner") reduces potential issues with substring matching in QA tests that check text content. This reduces confusion and minimizes the potential to break anything, so I'm leaving the CSS component commented. The only reason to add response time is for human moderators to resolve ties after the game. It is not currently needed.

**A Deep Dive into UI Consistency and Real-time Requirements**

Okay, so I've been digging into the UI design and requirements for this Quizzy project, and I think I've cracked it. I started by looking at the CSS, specifically `docs/mockups/quizzy.css` and the initial commit's styling for things like the result cards. I zeroed in on the styling for the `result-card__prefix` and realized a potential gotcha: using `display: block` with a prefix span could introduce unwanted newlines in the displayed text in Chromium. That would break the tests.

Thinking about the prompt's requirement for "Place 2 of 5" and how that's tested currently in `test/system/live_game_test.rb`, I need to make sure QA tests for `getByText("Place 2 of 5")` or `innerText.includes("Place 2 of 5")` still pass, regardless of how the DOM is structured.

I considered a few different DOM structures. The initial setup had issues, but I came up with an updated structure that seems perfect: a visually prominent display number using `aria-hidden="true"`, then a standard label like "Place 2 of 5", a score, and a banner if the player won. This new structure gets rid of the need for `display: block` and it’s much cleaner. The best part is that this setup will allow for easy matching for the QA tests.

Then, I looked at the "quiz is over" scenario, and realized that we're already testing this in `test/system/live_game_test.rb`. I saw a clear opportunity to keep the UI consistent across the big screen and player phones by displaying "The quiz is over" at the end of the quiz. This design would easily ensure that QA tests pass by putting "The quiz is over" as a text node in the DOM.

Finally, I got to the real-time latency requirement. I re-read the paragraph about speed deciding ties and how everything must be synced as close to instantly as possible. This means I need to carefully audit the entire real-time delivery pipeline to identify and remove any bottlenecks. I’ll start by reviewing how ActionCable is configured, specifically by looking at the settings for the development, test and production environments to see the adapter settings in `config/cable.yml` and related configuration files.

*   Broadcast each player's individual result on `game_player:<game_id>:<player_id>`. This gets each player their place, points, and winner status.

class Game < ApplicationRecord
  class NoActiveQuestionsError < StandardError; end

  STATUSES = %w[lobby question_open question_closed ended].freeze
  CODE_ALPHABET = "ABCDEFGHJKLMNPQRSTUVWXYZ23456789".chars.freeze
  CODE_LENGTH = 5

  belongs_to :quiz
  has_many :answers, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :players, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :game_questions, -> { order(:position, :id) }, dependent: :destroy

  validates :code, presence: true, uniqueness: true
  validates :status, presence: true, inclusion: { in: STATUSES }

  after_destroy_commit { GamePresence.clear_game(id) }

  def self.start_for_quiz!(quiz)
    active = quiz.active_questions.to_a
    raise NoActiveQuestionsError, "Add or activate at least one question before starting a game." if active.empty?

    transaction do
      game = quiz.games.create!(code: generate_unique_code, status: "lobby")

      active.each_with_index do |question, q_index|
        game_question = game.game_questions.create!(
          source_question_id: question.id,
          body: question.body,
          position: q_index + 1
        )

        question.options.ordered.each_with_index do |option, o_index|
          game_question.game_options.create!(
            source_option_id: option.id,
            body: option.body,
            correct: option.correct?,
            position: o_index + 1
          )
        end
      end

      game
    end
  end

  def self.generate_unique_code
    loop do
      candidate = Array.new(CODE_LENGTH) { CODE_ALPHABET[SecureRandom.random_number(CODE_ALPHABET.length)] }.join
      return candidate unless exists?(code: candidate)
    end
  end

  def lobby?
    status == "lobby"
  end

  def question_open?
    status == "question_open"
  end

  def question_closed?
    status == "question_closed"
  end

  def ended?
    status == "ended"
  end

  def winners_count
    quiz.number_of_winners
  end

  def ordered_game_questions
    game_questions.ordered.includes(:game_options)
  end

  def total_questions_count
    game_questions.count
  end

  def current_game_question
    return nil if current_question_index.nil?

    game_questions.ordered.includes(:game_options).offset(current_question_index).first
  end

  def current_question_number
    return nil if current_question_index.nil?

    current_question_index + 1
  end

  def last_question?
    return false if current_question_index.nil?

    current_question_index >= total_questions_count - 1
  end

  def active_players_count
    GamePresence.active_count(id)
  end

  def current_answers_count
    question = current_game_question
    return 0 unless question

    question.answers.count
  end

  def leaderboard_entries
    all_players = players.order(:id).to_a
    return [] if all_players.empty?

    opened_at_by_qid = game_questions.pluck(:id, :opened_at).to_h
    correct_answers = answers
      .joins(:game_option)
      .where(game_options: { correct: true })
      .pluck(:player_id, :game_question_id, :answered_at)

    points_by_player = Hash.new(0)
    time_us_by_player = Hash.new(0)

    correct_answers.each do |player_id, question_id, answered_at|
      points_by_player[player_id] += 1
      opened_at = opened_at_by_qid[question_id]
      if opened_at && answered_at
        elapsed_us = ((answered_at.to_r - opened_at.to_r) * 1_000_000).round
        time_us_by_player[player_id] += elapsed_us if elapsed_us.positive?
      end
    end

    ranked = all_players.sort_by do |player|
      [
        -points_by_player[player.id],
        time_us_by_player[player.id],
        player.id
      ]
    end

    ranked.each_with_index.map do |player, index|
      {
        player_id: player.id,
        place: index + 1,
        name: player.name,
        points: points_by_player[player.id],
        winner: player.winner?
      }
    end
  end

  def start!(expected_version: nil)
    transitioned = false

    transaction do
      reload
      next if version_mismatch?(expected_version)
      next unless lobby?
      next unless game_questions.exists?

      now = Time.current
      update!(
        status: "question_open",
        current_question_index: 0,
        state_version: state_version + 1,
        started_at: now,
        current_question_opened_at: now
      )
      current_game_question.update!(opened_at: now)
      transitioned = true
    end

    broadcast_state! if transitioned
    transitioned
  end

  def finish!(expected_version: nil)
    transitioned = false

    transaction do
      reload
      next if version_mismatch?(expected_version)
      next unless question_open?

      now = Time.current
      update!(
        status: "question_closed",
        state_version: state_version + 1
      )
      current_game_question&.update!(closed_at: now)
      transitioned = true
    end

    broadcast_state! if transitioned
    transitioned
  end

  def next_question!(expected_version: nil)
    transitioned = false

    transaction do
      reload
      next if version_mismatch?(expected_version)
      next unless question_closed? && !last_question?

      now = Time.current
      update!(
        status: "question_open",
        current_question_index: current_question_index + 1,
        state_version: state_version + 1,
        current_question_opened_at: now
      )
      current_game_question.update!(opened_at: now)
      transitioned = true
    end

    broadcast_state! if transitioned
    transitioned
  end

  def end_game!(expected_version: nil)
    transitioned = false

    transaction do
      reload
      next if version_mismatch?(expected_version)
      next unless question_closed? && last_question?

      now = Time.current
      update!(
        status: "ended",
        state_version: state_version + 1,
        ended_at: now
      )
      transitioned = true
    end

    broadcast_ended_state!(include_public: true) if transitioned
    transitioned
  end

  def pick_top_winners!
    changed = false

    transaction do
      reload
      next unless ended?

      entries = leaderboard_entries
      winner_ids = top_winner_ids(entries, winners_count)
      apply_winners!(winner_ids)
      changed = true
    end

    broadcast_ended_state!(include_public: false) if changed
    changed
  end

  def draw_winners!(random: SecureRandom)
    changed = false

    transaction do
      reload
      next unless ended?

      entries = leaderboard_entries
      winner_ids = drawn_winner_ids(entries, winners_count, random: random)
      apply_winners!(winner_ids)
      changed = true
    end

    broadcast_ended_state!(include_public: false) if changed
    changed
  end

  def reset_winners!
    changed = false

    transaction do
      reload
      next unless ended?

      apply_winners!([])
      changed = true
    end

    broadcast_ended_state!(include_public: false) if changed
    changed
  end

  def record_answer!(player:, game_question_id:, game_option_id:)
    received_at = Time.current
    saved_question_id = nil
    saved_option_id = nil

    transaction do
      reload
      next unless question_open?

      question = current_game_question
      next unless question && question.id == game_question_id.to_i

      option = question.game_options.find_by(id: game_option_id.to_i)
      next unless option

      answered_at = [ received_at, question.opened_at ].compact.max
      upsert_answer!(player: player, question: question, option: option, answered_at: answered_at)
      saved_question_id = question.id
      saved_option_id = option.id
    end

    if saved_option_id
      broadcast_moderator_counts!
      broadcast_player_answer!(player, saved_question_id, saved_option_id)
      { ok: true, game_question_id: saved_question_id, selected_option_id: saved_option_id }
    else
      { ok: false, state: player_state_for(player) }
    end
  end

  def moderator_state(join_url: nil, entries: nil)
    question = (question_open? || question_closed?) ? current_game_question : nil
    total = total_questions_count
    build_moderator_state(question: question, total: total, join_url: join_url, entries: entries)
  end

  def public_state
    question = (question_open? || question_closed?) ? current_game_question : nil
    total = total_questions_count
    build_public_state(question: question, total: total)
  end

  def player_state_for(player, entries: nil)
    question = (question_open? || question_closed?) ? current_game_question : nil
    total = total_questions_count
    state = build_public_state(question: question, total: total).merge(
      player_name: player.name,
      selected_option_id: nil
    )

    if question && (question_open? || question_closed?)
      selected_option_id = Answer.where(player_id: player.id, game_question_id: question.id).pick(:game_option_id)
      state[:selected_option_id] = selected_option_id

      if question_closed?
        state[:outcome] =
          if selected_option_id.nil?
            "none"
          elsif question.game_options.any? { |opt| opt.id == selected_option_id && opt.correct? }
            "correct"
          else
            "wrong"
          end
      end
    elsif ended?
      entries ||= leaderboard_entries
      entry = entries.find { |item| item[:player_id] == player.id }
      if entry
        state[:place] = entry[:place]
        state[:total_players] = entries.size
        state[:points] = entry[:points]
        state[:winner] = entry[:winner]
      end
    end

    state
  end

  def moderator_stream_name
    "game_moderator:#{id}"
  end

  def public_stream_name
    "game_public:#{id}"
  end

  def player_stream_name(player)
    "game_player:#{id}:#{player.id}"
  end

  def broadcast_state!
    if ended?
      broadcast_ended_state!(include_public: true)
      return
    end

    question = (question_open? || question_closed?) ? current_game_question : nil
    total = total_questions_count
    pub_state = build_public_state(question: question, total: total)
    mod_state = build_moderator_state(question: question, total: total)

    ActionCable.server.broadcast(public_stream_name, pub_state)
    ActionCable.server.broadcast(moderator_stream_name, mod_state)
  end

  def broadcast_moderator_state!
    ActionCable.server.broadcast(moderator_stream_name, moderator_state)
  end

  def broadcast_ended_state!(include_public: false)
    entries = leaderboard_entries
    total_players = entries.size
    total_questions = total_questions_count
    base_public = build_public_state(question: nil, total: total_questions)
    mod_state = build_moderator_state(question: nil, total: total_questions, entries: entries)

    ActionCable.server.broadcast(moderator_stream_name, mod_state)

    entries.each do |entry|
      personal_payload = base_public.merge(
        player_name: entry[:name],
        selected_option_id: nil,
        place: entry[:place],
        total_players: total_players,
        points: entry[:points],
        winner: entry[:winner]
      )
      ActionCable.server.broadcast("game_player:#{id}:#{entry[:player_id]}", personal_payload)
    end

    ActionCable.server.broadcast(public_stream_name, base_public) if include_public
  end

  def broadcast_moderator_counts!
    ActionCable.server.broadcast(
      moderator_stream_name,
      {
        type: "counts",
        state_version: state_version,
        active_players_count: active_players_count,
        answers_count: current_answers_count
      }
    )
  end

  def broadcast_player_answer!(player, game_question_id, game_option_id)
    ActionCable.server.broadcast(
      player_stream_name(player),
      {
        type: "player_answer",
        game_question_id: game_question_id,
        selected_option_id: game_option_id
      }
    )
  end

  private

  def build_moderator_state(question:, total:, join_url: nil, entries: nil)
    answers_count = question ? question.answers.count : 0

    payload = {
      type: "state",
      status: status,
      state_version: state_version,
      code: code,
      quiz_title: quiz.title,
      winners_count: winners_count,
      active_players_count: active_players_count,
      answers_count: answers_count,
      question_number: current_question_number,
      total_questions: total,
      last_question: current_question_index.present? && current_question_index >= total - 1,
      question: nil
    }
    payload[:join_url] = join_url if join_url.present?

    if question && (question_open? || question_closed?)
      option_counts = question_closed? ? question.answers.group(:game_option_id).count : {}
      total_answers = option_counts.values.sum

      payload[:question] = {
        id: question.id,
        body: question.body,
        options: question.game_options.ordered.map do |opt|
          item = {
            id: opt.id,
            position: opt.position,
            body: opt.body
          }
          if question_closed?
            count = option_counts.fetch(opt.id, 0)
            item[:correct] = opt.correct?
            item[:count] = count
            item[:share] = total_answers.positive? ? ((count * 100.0) / total_answers).round(1) : 0
          end
          item
        end
      }
    elsif ended?
      entries ||= leaderboard_entries
      payload[:leaderboard] = entries
      payload[:has_winners] = entries.any? { |entry| entry[:winner] }
    end

    payload
  end

  def build_public_state(question:, total:)
    payload = {
      type: "state",
      status: status,
      state_version: state_version,
      quiz_title: quiz.title,
      question_number: current_question_number,
      total_questions: total,
      question: nil
    }

    if question && (question_open? || question_closed?)
      payload[:question] = {
        id: question.id,
        body: question.body,
        options: question.game_options.ordered.map do |opt|
          item = {
            id: opt.id,
            position: opt.position,
            body: opt.body
          }
          # Never reveal correct options before the question is closed.
          item[:correct] = opt.correct? if question_closed?
          item
        end
      }
    end

    payload
  end

  def top_winner_ids(entries, count)
    entries.select { |entry| entry[:points].positive? }.first(count).map { |entry| entry[:player_id] }
  end

  def drawn_winner_ids(entries, count, random: SecureRandom)
    eligible = entries.select { |entry| entry[:points].positive? }
    return [] if eligible.empty?
    return eligible.map { |entry| entry[:player_id] } if eligible.size <= count

    cutoff_points = eligible[count - 1][:points]
    guaranteed = eligible.select { |entry| entry[:points] > cutoff_points }
    remaining = count - guaranteed.size
    tied_at_cutoff = eligible.select { |entry| entry[:points] == cutoff_points }
    drawn = tied_at_cutoff.sample(remaining, random: random)

    (guaranteed + drawn).map { |entry| entry[:player_id] }
  end

  def apply_winners!(winner_ids)
    players.update_all(winner: false)
    players.where(id: winner_ids).update_all(winner: true) if winner_ids.any?
    update!(state_version: state_version + 1)
  end

  def version_mismatch?(expected_version)
    expected_version.present? && state_version != expected_version.to_i
  end

  def upsert_answer!(player:, question:, option:, answered_at: Time.current)
    answer = Answer.find_or_initialize_by(player_id: player.id, game_question_id: question.id)
    answer.game_id = id
    answer.game_option_id = option.id
    answer.answered_at = answered_at
    answer.save!
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique
    existing = Answer.find_by!(player_id: player.id, game_question_id: question.id)
    existing.update!(game_option_id: option.id, answered_at: answered_at)
  end
end

class PlaysController < ApplicationController
  CLIENT_TOKEN_COOKIE = :quizzy_client_token

  before_action :set_game
  before_action :disable_caching

    @player = current_player_for(@game)

    end

    if @game.reload.ended?

    end

    if @player.save
      redirect_to play_path(@game.code), status: :see_other
    else
      render :join, status: :unprocessable_entity
    end
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique
    redirect_to play_path(@game.code), status: :see_other
  end

  def answer
    @player = current_player_for(@game)
    unless @player
      return respond_to do |format|
        format.json { render json: { error: "Join the game first" }, status: :unauthorized }
        format.html { redirect_to play_path(@game.code), status: :see_other }
      end
    end

    result = @game.record_answer!(
      player: @player,
      game_question_id: params[:game_question_id],
      game_option_id: params[:game_option_id]
    )

    if result[:ok]
      respond_to do |format|
        format.json { render json: result, status: :ok }
        format.html { redirect_to play_path(@game.code), status: :see_other }
      end
    else
      respond_to do |format|
        format.json { render json: result[:state], status: :conflict }
        format.html { redirect_to play_path(@game.code), status: :see_other }
      end
    end
  end

  def state
    @player = current_player_for(@game)

    if @player
      if params[:fallback] == "1" && !@game.ended?
        changed, _count = GamePresence.touch_http(@game.id, @player.id)
        @game.broadcast_moderator_counts! if changed
      end
      render json: @game.player_state_for(@player)
    else
      render json: @game.public_state
    end
  end

  private

  def set_game
    @game = Game.find_by!(code: params[:code].to_s.upcase)
  end

  def disable_caching
    response.headers["Cache-Control"] = "no-store"
  end

  def current_client_token
    cookies.signed[CLIENT_TOKEN_COOKIE].presence
  end

  def ensure_client_token
    token = current_client_token
    return token if token.present?

    token = SecureRandom.urlsafe_base64(24)
    cookies.signed[CLIENT_TOKEN_COOKIE] = {
      value: token,
      httponly: true,
      same_site: :lax,
      expires: 30.days.from_now
    }
    token
  end

  def current_player_for(game)
    token = current_client_token
    return nil if token.blank?

    game.players.find_by(client_token: token)
  end
end

class GamePlayerChannel < ApplicationCable::Channel
  def subscribed
    @game = Game.find_by(code: params[:code].to_s.upcase)
    @player = Player.find_signed(params[:token], purpose: :player_stream)
    return reject unless @game && @player && @player.game_id == @game.id

    @presence_connection_id = SecureRandom.hex(8)

    stream_from @game.public_stream_name
    stream_from @game.player_stream_name(@player)

    @presence_registered = true
    changed, _count = GamePresence.connect(@game.id, @player.id, @presence_connection_id)
    @game.reload

    transmit @game.player_state_for(@player)
    @game.broadcast_moderator_counts! if changed && !@game.ended?
  end

  def unsubscribed
    return unless @presence_registered && @game && @player

    @presence_registered = false
    changed, _count = GamePresence.disconnect(@game.id, @player.id, @presence_connection_id)
    if changed
      game = Game.find_by(id: @game.id)
      game.broadcast_moderator_counts! if game && !game.ended?
    end
  end
end

module ApplicationHelper
  def option_letter(index)
    return ("A".ord + index).chr if index < 26

    first = ("A".ord + (index / 26) - 1).chr
    second = ("A".ord + (index % 26)).chr
    "#{first}#{second}"
  end

    count = points.to_i

First, I'm noting the initial version check: I only update if `nextVersion` is greater than or equal to `currentVersion`. Crucial for preventing regressions. Next, the code carefully determines if the screen needs a full re-render based on if it's the `sameScreen`. I see this is checking `status`, `question.id`, and `endedSignature`.

Now, let's step through specific use cases: If the game transitions from a "question_closed" status to "ended," the `sameScreen` condition fails, prompting a full leaderboard render. Let's see how that works. A moderator clicks "Top 3", the server returns `state_version: 8`, marking top 3 winners. The `endedSignature` now changes so it triggers a re-render. After the first WS event triggers the change immediately. A subsequent WS event with the same `state_version` will be skipped cleanly. Nice! What if the moderator clicks "Draw" on one tab while another tab (projector) is open? The second tab should re-render immediately thanks to the `endedSignature` check. Okay, that's what I want. It’s all covered by properly queued websocket messages. We also checked how game start time is set with `started_at` in `Game#start!` and the question opens, and how this relates to timestamp calculation to minimize clock skew for players.

We confirmed that players never see their points during the game by examining the states across all screens. No `points`, `score`, or `place` keys. The check covers states: `lobby`, `question_open`, `question_closed`, the join page, and any WebSocket payloads.

We reviewed the `async` adapter in production, confirmed it's single-process with Puma (which it is), checked the WebSocket connections over different hostnames and the same-origin policy, including scenarios where a reverse proxy might be in place. We validated that the `ActionCable` consumer in the controllers connects immediately on page load and can handle any rapid game transitions that might occur before WebSocket subscription. We double-checked for any race conditions with how messages are streamed and transmitted to ensure messages are not missed.

We ensured screen readers won't read hidden, giant numeric rankings. We dissected the winning logic: the "Top N" button, the "Draw" button, and "Reset winners".     quiz = create_quiz_with_active_question

    assert_response :unauthorized

    assert_response :unauthorized

    assert_response :unauthorized

    post finish_moderate_game_path(game)
    assert_response :unauthorized

    post next_moderate_game_path(game)
    assert_response :unauthorized

    post end_moderate_game_path(game)
    assert_response :unauthorized
  end

  test "creating a game with no active questions redirects back with alert" do
    quiz = Quiz.create!(title: "No Active Questions")
    post moderate_quiz_games_path(quiz), headers: basic_auth_headers
    assert_redirected_to moderate_quiz_path(quiz)
    assert_equal 0, Game.count
  end

  test "player endpoints are public, remember player per game, and never leak correct answer while open" do
    quiz = create_quiz_with_active_question
    game = Game.start_for_quiz!(quiz)

    # Join page works without auth (case-insensitive code)
    get play_path(game.code.downcase)

    assert_includes response.body, "Join"

    # Blank name rejected
    post join_play_path(game.code), params: { player: { name: "   " } }
    assert_response :unprocessable_entity

    # Valid join remembers player via signed cookie

require "test_helper"

class GameScoringAndWinnersTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  def create_quiz(winners: 3, question_count: 3)
    quiz = Quiz.create!(title: "Prizes Quiz", number_of_winners: winners)
    question_count.times do |i|
      q = quiz.questions.build(body: "Question #{i + 1}?", active: true)
      q.save_with_option_rows([
        { body: "Correct A", correct: true },
        { body: "Correct B", correct: true },
        { body: "Wrong C", correct: false }
      ])
    end
    quiz
  end

  def option_by_body(question, body)
    question.game_options.find_by!(body: body)
  end

  test "scores 1 point per correct answer, ranks ties by lower total correct answer time using last pick, and excludes wrong answer times" do
    quiz = create_quiz(winners: 3, question_count: 2)
    game = Game.start_for_quiz!(quiz)

    alice = game.players.create!(name: "Alice", client_token: "a")
    bob = game.players.create!(name: "Bob", client_token: "b")
    charlie = game.players.create!(name: "Charlie", client_token: "c")
    dave = game.players.create!(name: "Dave", client_token: "d")
    eve = game.players.create!(name: "Eve", client_token: "e")

    base = Time.zone.parse("2026-11-21 12:00:00")

    # Question 1
    travel_to(base) { game.start! }
    q1 = game.reload.current_game_question

    # Alice picks correct early (+1s), then changes to wrong (+2s), then back to correct (+5s) -> last pick is +5s
    travel_to(base + 1.second) { game.record_answer!(player: alice, game_question_id: q1.id, game_option_id: option_by_body(q1, "Correct A").id) }
    travel_to(base + 2.seconds) { game.record_answer!(player: alice, game_question_id: q1.id, game_option_id: option_by_body(q1, "Wrong C").id) }
    travel_to(base + 5.seconds) { game.record_answer!(player: alice, game_question_id: q1.id, game_option_id: option_by_body(q1, "Correct B").id) }

    # Bob picks correct at +3s
    travel_to(base + 3.seconds) { game.record_answer!(player: bob, game_question_id: q1.id, game_option_id: option_by_body(q1, "Correct A").id) }

    # Charlie picks wrong very slowly (+20s) -> must NOT count toward Charlie's correct answer time!
    travel_to(base + 20.seconds) { game.record_answer!(player: charlie, game_question_id: q1.id, game_option_id: option_by_body(q1, "Wrong C").id) }

    # Dave picks wrong at +0.5s -> 0 points
    travel_to(base + 0.5.seconds) { game.record_answer!(player: dave, game_question_id: q1.id, game_option_id: option_by_body(q1, "Wrong C").id) }

    # Eve does not answer Q1

    # During open & closed question, players must NOT see points or leaderboard
    assert_not game.player_state_for(alice).key?(:points)
    assert_not game.player_state_for(alice).key?(:place)
    assert_not game.player_state_for(alice).key?(:winner)

    travel_to(base + 25.seconds) { game.finish! }
    assert_not game.player_state_for(alice).key?(:points)
    assert_not game.player_state_for(alice).key?(:place)
    assert_not game.player_state_for(alice).key?(:winner)

    # Question 2 opens at base + 30s
    q2_open = base + 30.seconds
    travel_to(q2_open) { game.next_question! }
    q2 = game.reload.current_game_question

    # Alice picks correct at +1s -> total correct time: 5s + 1s = 6s (2 points)
    travel_to(q2_open + 1.second) { game.record_answer!(player: alice, game_question_id: q2.id, game_option_id: option_by_body(q2, "Correct A").id) }

    # Bob picks correct at +4s -> total correct time: 3s + 4s = 7s (2 points) -> Alice (6s) beats Bob (7s)!
    travel_to(q2_open + 4.seconds) { game.record_answer!(player: bob, game_question_id: q2.id, game_option_id: option_by_body(q2, "Correct B").id) }

    # Charlie picks correct at +1.5s -> total correct time: 1.5s (1 point; Q1 wrong +20s excluded!)
    travel_to(q2_open + 1.5.seconds) { game.record_answer!(player: charlie, game_question_id: q2.id, game_option_id: option_by_body(q2, "Correct A").id) }

    quiz = create_quiz(winners: 3, question_count: 1)
    game = Game.start_for_quiz!(quiz)
    game.players.create!(name: "ZeroA", client_token: "a")
    game.players.create!(name: "ZeroB", client_token: "b")

    game.start!
    game.finish!
    game.end_game!

    game.pick_top_winners!
    assert_equal 0, game.players.where(winner: true).count

    game.draw_winners!
    assert_equal 0, game.players.where(winner: true).count
  end

  test "Draw guarantees players above N-th place points and randomly draws remaining prizes among players tied at N-th place points regardless of speed" do
    quiz = create_quiz(winners: 3, question_count: 3)
    game = Game.start_for_quiz!(quiz)

    # 1st: Alice (3 pts) -> strictly above cutoff (1 pt) -> ALWAYS wins
    # 2nd: Bob (2 pts) -> strictly above cutoff (1 pt) -> ALWAYS wins
    # 3rd-5th: Charlie (1 pt, 1s), Dave (1 pt, 2s), Eve (1 pt, 3s) -> tied at 3rd place's points (1 pt) -> 1 drawn at random!
    # 6th: Frank (0 pts) -> NEVER wins
    alice = game.players.create!(name: "Alice", client_token: "a")
    bob = game.players.create!(name: "Bob", client_token: "b")
    charlie = game.players.create!(name: "Charlie", client_token: "c")
    dave = game.players.create!(name: "Dave", client_token: "d")
    eve = game.players.create!(name: "Eve", client_token: "e")
    frank = game.players.create!(name: "Frank", client_token: "f")

    base = Time.zone.parse("2026-11-21 12:00:00")

    # Q1: Alice, Bob, Charlie, Dave, Eve get it right (at different speeds)
    travel_to(base) { game.start! }
    q1 = game.reload.current_game_question
    c1 = option_by_body(q1, "Correct A")
    travel_to(base + 1.second) { game.record_answer!(player: alice, game_question_id: q1.id, game_option_id: c1.id) }
    travel_to(base + 1.second) { game.record_answer!(player: bob, game_question_id: q1.id, game_option_id: c1.id) }
    travel_to(base + 1.second) { game.record_answer!(player: charlie, game_question_id: q1.id, game_option_id: c1.id) }
    travel_to(base + 2.seconds) { game.record_answer!(player: dave, game_question_id: q1.id, game_option_id: c1.id) }
    travel_to(base + 3.seconds) { game.record_answer!(player: eve, game_question_id: q1.id, game_option_id: c1.id) }
    travel_to(base + 5.seconds) { game.finish! }

    # Q2: Alice, Bob get it right
    travel_to(base + 10.seconds) { game.next_question! }
    q2 = game.reload.current_game_question
    c2 = option_by_body(q2, "Correct A")
    travel_to(base + 11.seconds) { game.record_answer!(player: alice, game_question_id: q2.id, game_option_id: c2.id) }
    travel_to(base + 11.seconds) { game.record_answer!(player: bob, game_question_id: q2.id, game_option_id: c2.id) }
    travel_to(base + 15.seconds) { game.finish! }

    # Q3: Alice gets it right
    travel_to(base + 20.seconds) { game.next_question! }
    q3 = game.reload.current_game_question
    c3 = option_by_body(q3, "Correct A")
    travel_to(base + 21.seconds) { game.record_answer!(player: alice, game_question_id: q3.id, game_option_id: c3.id) }
    travel_to(base + 25.seconds) { game.finish! }
    travel_to(base + 26.seconds) { game.end_game! }

    # Verify Top 3 picks Alice, Bob, Charlie (fastest of 1-pt players)
    game.pick_top_winners!
    assert_equal [ alice.id, bob.id, charlie.id ].sort, game.players.where(winner: true).pluck(:id).sort

    # Verify Draw over 30 draws: Alice & Bob ALWAYS win, Frank NEVER wins, and all 3 tied players (Charlie, Dave, Eve) get picked at least once
    drawn_third = Set.new
    rng = Random.new(12345)
    30.times do
      game.draw_winners!(random: rng)
      winners = game.players.where(winner: true).pluck(:id)
      assert_equal 3, winners.size
      assert_includes winners, alice.id
      assert_includes winners, bob.id
      assert_not_includes winners, frank.id
      third = (winners - [ alice.id, bob.id ]).first
      assert_includes [ charlie.id, dave.id, eve.id ], third
      drawn_third.add(third)
    end

    assert_equal Set[ charlie.id, dave.id, eve.id ], drawn_third
  end

  test "Draw handles all players tied at 1st place (nobody strictly above cutoff)" do
    quiz = create_quiz(winners: 2, question_count: 1)
    game = Game.start_for_quiz!(quiz)
    players = 4.times.map { |i| game.players.create!(name: "P#{i + 1}", client_token: "t#{i}") }

    base = Time.zone.parse("2026-11-21 12:00:00")
    travel_to(base) { game.start! }
    q1 = game.reload.current_game_question
    c1 = option_by_body(q1, "Correct A")
    players.each_with_index do |p, idx|
      travel_to(base + (idx + 1).seconds) { game.record_answer!(player: p, game_question_id: q1.id, game_option_id: c1.id) }
    end
    travel_to(base + 10.seconds) { game.finish! }
    travel_to(base + 11.seconds) { game.end_game! }

    # Even the fastest player (P1) is in the random pool because nobody has MORE points than 2nd place!
    seen_sets = Set.new
    rng = Random.new(999)
    30.times do
      game.draw_winners!(random: rng)
      winners = game.players.where(winner: true).pluck(:id).sort
      assert_equal 2, winners.size
      seen_sets.add(winners)
    end

    assert_operator seen_sets.size, :>, 1
    assert seen_sets.any? { |s| !s.include?(players[0].id) }, "Fastest player should not be guaranteed when tied on points"
  end

  test "Draw handles game with 0 players gracefully" do
    quiz = create_quiz(winners: 3, question_count: 1)
    game = Game.start_for_quiz!(quiz)
    game.start!
    game.finish!
    game.end_game!

    assert_equal [], game.leaderboard_entries
    assert game.pick_top_winners!
    assert game.draw_winners!
    assert game.reset_winners!
  end
end

module GameChannelTestHelper

end

class GameModeratorChannelTest < ActionCable::Channel::TestCase
  include GameChannelTestHelper
  tests GameModeratorChannel

  test "requires valid signed token and transmits state including ended leaderboard" do
    game = create_game(winners: 2)

    subscribe(token: "invalid-token")
    assert subscription.rejected?

    token = game.signed_id(purpose: :moderator_stream)
    subscribe(token: token)
    assert subscription.confirmed?
    assert_has_stream game.moderator_stream_name
    assert_equal "lobby", transmissions.last[:status]
    assert_equal 2, transmissions.last[:winners_count]

    unsubscribe

    alice = game.players.create!(name: "Alice", client_token: "a")

    game.pick_top_winners!

    subscribe(token: token)
    assert subscription.confirmed?
    ended_payload = transmissions.last
    assert_equal "ended", ended_payload[:status]
    assert_equal 2, ended_payload[:winners_count]
    assert_equal 1, ended_payload[:leaderboard].size
    assert_equal true, ended_payload[:leaderboard][0][:winner]
  end
end

class GamePlayerChannelTest < ActionCable::Channel::TestCase
  include GameChannelTestHelper
  tests GamePlayerChannel

  test "tracks presence, transmits safe player state, and transmits place/points/winner after end" do
    game = create_game
    player = game.players.create!(name: "Alice", client_token: "tok-a")
    game.start!

    subscribe(code: game.code, token: "bad")
    assert subscription.rejected?
    assert_equal 0, GamePresence.active_count(game.id)

    subscribe(code: game.code, token: token)

    assert_equal "ended", ended_payload[:status]
    assert_equal 1, ended_payload[:place]
    assert_equal 1, ended_payload[:total_players]
    assert_equal 1, ended_payload[:points]
    assert_equal true, ended_payload[:winner]
  end

The same needs to occur on each players phones. I'll need to use `innerText` to ensure no weird newline splitting issues.

- `GET /up` serves the unauthenticated Rails health check (`200 OK`).
- All persistent data lives under `storage/`.

## Authentication

- All moderator routes live under `/moderate` and inherit from `Moderate::BaseController`.
- `Moderate::BaseController` enforces HTTP Basic authentication against `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME` and `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD` using constant-time SHA-256 digest comparison (`ActiveSupport::SecurityUtils.secure_compare`). Empty/missing env vars reject with `401`.
- Because browsers do not send HTTP Basic credentials to `/cable`, `GameModeratorChannel` authenticates via a cryptographic signed token (`game.signed_id(purpose: :moderator_stream, expires_in: 24.hours)`) issued by `Moderate::GamesController#show`.
- Public player routes live under `/play/:code` (`PlaysController`) and do not require moderator credentials. Players are remembered per browser via an HTTP-only signed cookie (`quizzy_client_token`, `same_site: :lax`, no `secure` flag so plain HTTP works on any host) paired with `players(game_id, client_token)`.

### Quiz Authoring
- `Quiz` (`quizzes`: `title`) `has_many :questions, dependent: :destroy`, `has_many :games, dependent: :destroy`
- `Question` (`questions`: `quiz_id`, `body`, `position`, `active`) `has_many :options, dependent: :destroy`
- `Option` (`options`: `question_id`, `body`, `correct`, `position`)

### Live Games
- `Game` (`games`: `quiz_id`, `code` unique 5-char unambiguous uppercase code, `status` in `lobby|question_open|question_closed|ended`, `current_question_index`, `state_version`, `started_at`, `current_question_opened_at`, `ended_at`).
- `GameQuestion` (`game_questions`: `game_id`, `source_question_id` informational, `body`, `position`, `opened_at`, `closed_at`). Active questions are snapshotted at `Game.start_for_quiz!(quiz)` so inactive questions are skipped and later quiz edits/deletes never break existing or historical games.
- `GameOption` (`game_options`: `game_question_id`, `source_option_id` informational, `body`, `correct`, `position`).
- `Player` (`players`: `game_id`, `name`, `client_token` unique per `game_id`).
- `Answer` (`answers`: `game_id`, `player_id`, `game_question_id`, `game_option_id`, `answered_at`, unique on `[player_id, game_question_id]`).

## Live Game Real-Time Architecture & Conference Wi-Fi Resilience

- **Channels**:
  - `GameModeratorChannel`: streams `game_moderator:<game_id>` (full moderator state + live `counts` updates) and transmits canonical state immediately on subscribe/reconnect.
  - `GamePlayerChannel`: authenticated via `player.signed_id(purpose: :player_stream)`, streams shared `game_public:<game_id>` (O(1) broadcast to all players) and personal `game_player:<game_id>:<player_id>` (multi-tab answer sync), registers/unregisters active presence in `GamePresence`, and transmits personal authoritative state on subscribe/reconnect.
  - `GamePublicChannel`: used on the unjoined `/play/:code` form so visitors live-transition to `"The quiz is over"` if the game ends while the join form is open, without being counted as active players.
- **Presence (`GamePresence`)**:
  - Thread-safe in-memory registry deduplicating multiple WebSocket connections per `(game_id, player_id)`. Closing a tab/socket immediately updates `Players: N` (lobby) and `Answers: X / Y` (open question).
  - Supports short HTTP leases (`touch_http`) exclusively for fallback-polling clients when WebSockets are blocked by conference networks.
- **No Answer Leakage**:
  - `Game#public_state` and `Game#player_state_for` strictly omit `correct` and `outcome` fields while `status == "question_open"`. Correct options are only included once `status == "question_closed"`.

  - State transitions use monotonic `state_version` with `expected_version` guards to prevent accidental double-click skips.
  - Answer submissions (`POST /play/:code/answer`) are serialized per client (`player_game_controller.js`) with automatic retry on transient network/5xx errors and `409 Conflict` state reconciliation if a question closes mid-flight.
  - Stimulus controllers implement jittered fast WebSocket reconnect (0.5s–5s backoff instead of ActionCable's 12–24s default) plus fallback HTTP state polling while disconnected and immediate sync on `online` / `visibilitychange`.

## Export & Import

- `Quiz::Exporter` (`app/models/quiz/exporter.rb`) serializes a quiz to pretty-printed JSON with **strictly** `title`, `questions` (`text`, `active`, `options` with `text`, `correct`). Live game models are intentionally excluded from export.
- `Quiz::Importer` (`app/models/quiz/importer.rb`) validates JSON syntax, types, and question rules atomically in a single transaction.

## Notes for Future Releases

- `GameQuestion#opened_at`, `GameQuestion#closed_at`, and `Answer#answered_at` are already persisted to support future leaderboards, response-time tie-breakers, and moderator run history/response breakdowns without schema migration friction.
- ActionCable currently uses the `async` adapter (single-process Puma). If multi-worker Puma is ever enabled, switch to `solid_cable` and back `GamePresence` with SQLite under `storage/`.
"
}

# Quizzy Architecture Notes

## Overview

Quizzy is a Ruby on Rails 8.1 application backed by SQLite (`storage/<env>.sqlite3`), Hotwire (Turbo + Stimulus via Importmap), ActionCable (`async` adapter over WebSockets), and Propshaft for local assets. All design assets (`app/assets/stylesheets/quizzy.css`, `app/assets/fonts/Inter-latin.woff2`) and QR codes (`rqrcode` generating inline HTML5 SVG) are served locally without external network dependencies.

- Production runs over plain HTTP (`force_ssl = false`, `assume_ssl = false`) and accepts any `Host` header (`config.hosts.clear`). ActionCable uses `allow_same_origin_as_host = true`, accepting WebSocket upgrades from any hostname over plain HTTP.
- `GET /up` serves the unauthenticated Rails health check (`200 OK`).
- All persistent data lives under `storage/`.

## Authentication

- All moderator routes live under `/moderate` and inherit from `Moderate::BaseController`.
- `Moderate::BaseController` enforces HTTP Basic authentication against `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME` and `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD` using constant-time SHA-256 digest comparison (`ActiveSupport::SecurityUtils.secure_compare`). Empty/missing env vars reject with `401`.

Players are remembered per browser via an HTTP-only signed cookie (`quizzy_client_token`, `same_site: :lax`, no `secure` flag so plain HTTP works on any host) paired with `players(game_id, client_token)`.

## Data Model

### Quiz Authoring
- `Quiz` (`quizzes`: `title`, `number_of_winners` default `3`, integer `>= 1`) `has_many :questions, dependent: :destroy`, `has_many :games, dependent: :destroy`
- `Question` (`questions`: `quiz_id`, `body`, `position`, `active`) `has_many :options, dependent: :destroy`
- `Option` (`options`: `question_id`, `body`, `correct`, `position`)

### Live Games
- `Game` (`games`: `quiz_id`, `code` unique 5-char unambiguous uppercase code, `status` in `lobby|question_open|question_closed|ended`, `current_question_index`, `state_version`, `started_at`, `current_question_opened_at`, `ended_at`).

- `Player` (`players`: `game_id`, `name`, `client_token` unique per `game_id`, `winner` boolean default `false`).
- `Answer` (`answers`: `game_id`, `player_id`, `game_question_id`, `game_option_id`, `answered_at`, unique on `[player_id, game_question_id]`).

- **Scoring (`Game#leaderboard_entries`)**:
  - 1 point per correct answer (`game_options.correct = true`).
  - Ties on points are broken by lower total time of **correct** answers only, calculated in exact integer microseconds from `game_questions.opened_at` to `answers.answered_at` (the player's last pick). Wrong answers and unanswered questions contribute 0 points and 0 time.
  - Remaining ties break deterministically by `players.id`.
  - Points, place, and winner status are omitted from player payloads during `lobby`, `question_open`, and `question_closed`, and revealed only when `status == "ended"`.
- **Winner Selection (`POST /moderate/games/:id/{top_winners,draw_winners,reset_winners}`)**:
  - Players with 0 points never win. If fewer than `N` (`quiz.number_of_winners`) players have points, all players with `points > 0` win.
  - `pick_top_winners!` ("Top N"): first `N` eligible players on the leaderboard win.
  - `draw_winners!` ("Draw"): every eligible player with strictly more points than the N-th place wins; remaining prizes are drawn uniformly at random (`SecureRandom`) among eligible players with exactly the N-th place's points (ignoring speed). Each click draws fresh winners.
  - `reset_winners!` ("Reset winners"): clears `players.winner = false` for all players in the game.
  - All winner mutations run inside a single transaction, bump `state_version`, and live-broadcast updated leaderboard state to the moderator screen and personal `{ place, total_players, points, winner }` payloads to every player's phone.

- **Channels**:

- **Presence (`GamePresence`)**:

  - `Game#public_state` and `Game#player_state_for` strictly omit `correct` and `outcome` fields while `status == "question_open"`, and strictly omit `points`, `place`, `total_players`, and `winner` until `status == "ended"`.

- `Quiz::Importer` (`app/models/quiz/importer.rb`) validates JSON syntax, types, and question rules atomically in a single transaction.
